officialAdobeApi.source: Adobe official Premiere CEP/ExtendScript and UXP documentation, inspected 2026-08-19

cepComponent.documentedIdentity: matchName uniquely identifies the effect plug-in, not a clip instance

cepTrackItem.documentedSelection: TrackItem.isSelected / Sequence.getSelection select clips, not Effect Controls rows
cepTrackItem.documentedId: TrackItem.nodeId is documented on TrackItem, not on Component

uxpComponent.paramIndexNote: UXP: Parameter indexes are zero-based, and the actual is defined exclusively by the component itself. That documents plugin-defined parameter order, not Lumetri instance identity and not Effect Controls selection.

uxpVideoComponentChain.indexSemantics: Index addresses a position in the component chain. Adobe does not document that this index equals the user's focused Effect Controls row, or that it is a stable unique instance id across reordering.

uxpSelection.sequenceGetSelection: Returns TrackItemSelection (clips), not a selected effect/component
uxpSelection.projectItemGetId: ProjectItem.getId() exists; Component has no getId()
uxpSelection.propertiesApi: Properties.getProperties(owner) is a named key/value bag on Project/Sequence/etc, not Component instance identity

officialAdobeApi.extendscriptFrozen: Premiere 23.0 scripting changelog: no further ExtendScript API improvements planned; future work is UXP.

conclusions.officialUniqueInstanceIdentity: not found on documented or probed fields
conclusions.componentIndexNote: trackItem.components[index] / UXP getComponentAtIndex(index) can target a specific chain position. Adobe does not document that position as the user's focused Lumetri, and reordering effects changes it.
conclusions.parameterIndexNote: Do not treat parameterIndex as semantic identity unless Adobe documents it or live values uniquely and stably identify the intended Saturation. UXP only says indexes are defined by the component itself.

note: This diagnostic never writes, never calls setValue/setValueAtKey/addKey, never uses QE, and never chooses first/last/index as the intended Lumetri.
